title: Traffic throttling contracts for heterogeneous canaries (draft)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working sketch of explicit throttling contracts for rolling out LLM changes where the canaries are heterogeneous: different model sizes, quantizations, or routing policies across endpoints. Goal: give oncall + release stewards a compact set of throttle rules that protect latency SLOs, stabilize cost, and keep user-visible errors rare while enabling progressive exposure.

Why this is needed (notes to self):
- We frequently see oscillation when a small percentage of traffic hits a heavier model variant (e.g., 2% hitting 2x cost). Without throttles, temporary traffic bursts (or poor partitioning) blow past budgets and trigger rapid rollbacks that block experiments.
- Heterogeneous canaries amplify risk because performance/cost signals are not directly comparable between variants. A naive percentage-based split disguises per-request resource imbalance.

Basic ideas (high level):
1) Bind canary exposure to two axes: slice-weight (user cohort %) and resource-rate (tokens/sec or active-rps) for the heavy variant.
2) Define explicit soft and hard throttles. Soft throttles slow growth and send alerts; hard throttles immediately cap or drain traffic to the safe baseline.
3) Tie throttles to cost/SLO budgets per release, not just global budgets. Each rollout has a small cost envelope and a latency budget for the canary cohort.

Concrete contract template (fill per-release):
- Canary variant id: (model:quant-profile:region)
- Target cohort(s): e.g., web-search-US, mobile-android-global
- Initial exposure: 0.5% or 100 rps (whichever smaller)
- Max exposure by day: 5% or 3x baseline rps per cohort
- Soft throttle trigger conditions (any one):
    * median p99 latency increase for cohort vs baseline > 35% for 5m window
    * token-cost/sec for canary variant > 2x baseline average sustained for 3m
    * error rate (5xx or model-fallbacks) > 0.5% absolute and +0.3pp relative increase
    * signal noise: variance of p50 latency > baseline variance * 2 for 10m
  Soft throttle action: cap incremental traffic growth to +0.1% per 30m for next 2 hours; create P0 alert to #canary-ops; run rollback dry-check (automated simulation).
- Hard throttle trigger conditions (any one):
    * p99 latency > SLO + 300ms for 2m continuous
    * token-cost/sec > 4x baseline OR cumulative canary cost > 120% of release envelope in 24h
    * catastrophic error spike: failure response ratio > 2% absolute for 1m
  Hard throttle action: revert traffic to baseline variant for cohort immediately; notify oncall and release owner; engage mitigation checklist.

Operational run scenarios (for playtests):
1) Burst traffic from a microfrontend during marketing spike. Simulate 5x baseline rps for 10m targeted at canary cohort. Expected: soft throttle triggers and caps growth; if sustained beyond 20m with cost spike, hard throttle should cutover.
2) Degraded GPUs in a specific AZ causing p99 tail to inflate for heavy quantized variant. Expected: p99 triggers soft then hard throttle if tail persists > 2m.
3) A/B confusion: model A lower latency but lower quality; model B provides better quality but twice the cost and slightly higher p99. Strategy: allow higher p50 increase if quality metrics (RER / eval set) improve beyond threshold; otherwise respect cost throttle.

Telemetry and dashboards (minimal set to implement):
- Per-cohort: p50/p90/p99 latency, request/sec, tokens/sec, error-rate, fallback-rate
- Per-variant: avg token cost, GPU utilization, queue-length, active-kv-entries
- Release envelope: cumulative cost for canary vs allocated budget in last 24h
- Throttle state timeline: events showing soft/hard throttle transitions + responsible actor (auto/manual)

Alerting + ownership:
- Soft-throttle alert -> #canary-ops (SRE + release PM + model owner) -> 15m ack SLA
- Hard-throttle alert -> oncall SRE + PagerDuty escalation -> immediate rollback automation allowed (configurable)
- Post-mortem owner: release PM

Manual override and experiment exceptions:
- Permission: product owners can request temporary throttle relaxation via a signed commit message and a single-approver oncall SRE. Record rationale and time-limited window.
- Short-lived experiments (under 2 hours) can opt out of cost throttle but not latency hard throttles. This must be declared before exposure.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Decide default numeric thresholds for our fleet (start conservative). Suggest: p99 increase threshold 35%, soft token-cost multiplier 2x, hard 4x. Request SRE input.
- How to measure "token-cost/sec" uniformly across quantized models (cost estimator function needed).
- Automate per-release envelope calculation (pull pricing/quant profile from model catalog). Ticket: REDW-4823.
- Decide retention for throttle timeline (30 days?) for post-launch analysis.
- Add synthetic probe traffic pattern for each cohort to ensure signal availability when traffic is sparse.

Quick checklist for release owner before enabling canary throttles:
- [ ] Register release with release-envelopes and set cost budget
- [ ] Identify cohorts and expected baseline traffic
- [ ] Attach model cost profile (from model-catalog)
- [ ] Create dashboard with the minimal telemetry widgets above
- [ ] Run a 10m synthetic smoke test to verify alerts and throttle automation behave as expected

Notes to collaborators:
- This is intentionally conservative. We want to avoid churn + surprise bills as the primary failure mode.
- Feedback welcome on threshold granularity or if people prefer percent-of-baseline rules only.
- If you see an edge-case where cohort-based throttles are infeasible (very low traffic cohorts), propose a synthetic probe policy (we can bind throttle to probe rate).

Slack references and quick links (for playtests):
- #canary-ops (ops watchroom)
- #release-sync (release owner comms)
- PagerDuty schedule: SRE-oncall

Signoff draft: Marisol Vega (product), Evan Brooks (SRE), Tom Nguyen (console infra)

Revision notes (2024-12-15): tightened soft throttle cap growth, added explicit change-log for manual override, added playtest scenarios.
